title: Product innovation and informal market competition in sub-Saharan Africa
summary: Competition from informal enterprises is one of the top three obstacles formal businesses face in sub-Saharan Africa. The paper finds that local informal competition harms the performance of product innovation, but only for formal firms that lack strategic collaborative footholds in the informal economy.
keyFindings: Local informal competition has a robust negative effect on the product innovation intensity of formal firms.
Informal competition within an industry enhances innovative sales.
Larger firms are less affected by local informal competition and gain innovative sales from it.
methods: World Bank Enterprise Surveys combined with the Innovation Follow-up Survey for five sub-Saharan African countries, with regional and industry-specific indicators of informal competition.
